meta.title: Setup Flows — Foreign Investment in Saudi Arabia
meta.description: Conceptual setup flows for common foreign investment scenarios in Saudi Arabia. All flows describe the typical sequence of authorizations and registrations at a conceptual level only — not procedural instructions, legal requirements, or approval guarantees. Steps reference concepts from other datasets in this repository.
meta.last_verified: placeholder — all flows are draft; verify every step against current official sources before relying on this sequence

data.name: Foreign Consulting Company Setup
data.short_description: Conceptual setup sequence for a foreign investor establishing a consulting or professional services company in Saudi Arabia as a limited liability company (LLC).
data.target_investor_type: Foreign investor establishing a consulting or professional services business in Saudi Arabia

steps.label: Activity eligibility verification
steps.description: Verify that the intended consulting activity is available to foreign investors. MISA maintains an activity classification list; the eligibility status of specific consulting sub-activities and any foreign ownership restrictions must be confirmed at the MISA portal before proceeding.
steps.notes: Activity eligibility may differ by consulting sub-sector. Confirm the specific MISA activity code applicable to the intended service type.

steps.label: Business structure selection
steps.description: Determine the appropriate legal structure: LLC (a locally incorporated Saudi entity with limited liability) or branch office of an existing foreign company (an extension of the parent with no separate legal personality). This flow assumes LLC structure.
steps.notes: Structure choice affects liability, ownership, minimum capital, and ongoing compliance. Verify current requirements for each structure at MISA and the Ministry of Commerce before finalising.

steps.label: MISA investment registration
steps.description: Submit an investment registration application to MISA for the authorized consulting activity. A successful application produces an investment registration certificate that authorizes the investor to establish a Saudi legal entity for the specified activities.

steps.label: Commercial registration
steps.description: Register the legal entity (LLC) with the Ministry of Commerce to obtain a commercial registration certificate (CR). The CR creates the legal person in the Saudi commercial register and is conceptually distinct from the MISA investment registration.

steps.label: Chamber of Commerce membership
steps.description: Complete Chamber of Commerce annual membership registration. Membership with the relevant local Chamber of Commerce is mandatory for all Saudi-registered companies and is required as part of the commercial registration process. The annual fee varies by company class (minimum SAR 800/year for Class 3).
steps.notes: Chamber of Commerce membership is not optional — it is required for CR issuance and ongoing compliance. The annual membership fee is a mandatory recurring cost that must be factored into the company's annual budget.

steps.label: Municipal operating license
steps.description: Obtain a Balady operating license for the physical premises from which the business will operate. This step applies to businesses with a physical office in Saudi Arabia and authorizes operation at a specific location.
steps.notes: Applies where a physical premises is maintained. Businesses operating without a fixed physical office should verify whether this step applies to their situation.

steps.label: Social insurance registration
steps.description: Register as an employer with GOSI before hiring any employees. GOSI registration is required for all employers operating in Saudi Arabia and must be completed before the first employee joins.

steps.label: Tax and Zakat registration
steps.description: Register with ZATCA for VAT, zakat, and income tax obligations applicable to the business. ZATCA registration must be completed within 60 days of commencing business activities — this is a statutory deadline. CIT applies to the foreign-owned portion of profits at 20%; Zakat applies to Saudi/GCC-owned portions at 2.5% of the Zakat base. VAT registration is required when taxable turnover meets the mandatory threshold.
steps.notes: 60-day registration deadline from business commencement is a statutory obligation. CIT rate: 20% of net adjusted profits. Zakat rate: 2.5% of Zakat base. Confirm current VAT registration thresholds at zatca.gov.sa.

steps.label: Labor platform registration and Saudization review
steps.description: Register as an employer on the Qiwa platform (qiwa.sa) before hiring any employees. Authenticate all employment contracts via Qiwa. Review Nitaqat (Saudization) obligations — the applicable band and minimum Saudi employee ratio depend on the business activity and workforce size. Register each expatriate employee's Iqama via Muqeem within 90 days of their arrival.
steps.notes: Qiwa employer registration must precede the first hire. Saudization obligations should be assessed before finalising the staffing plan. Confirm the applicable Nitaqat band for consulting activities via official channels.

decision_points.question: LLC or branch office of foreign company?
options: LLC — a locally incorporated Saudi entity; shareholders have limited liability; verify current minimum shareholder and capital requirements at MISA
Branch office — an extension of the foreign parent in Saudi Arabia; no separate legal personality; parent company bears liability for branch obligations

decision_points.question: Is a physical premises required?
options: Physical office maintained in Saudi Arabia — Balady municipal operating license required for the premises
No fixed physical premises — verify whether this step applies and how the registered address requirement can be satisfied

data.name: E-Commerce Company Setup
data.short_description: Conceptual setup sequence for a foreign investor establishing an e-commerce business in Saudi Arabia, covering the core registration path and key conditional steps for product compliance and physical warehousing.
data.target_investor_type: Foreign investor establishing an e-commerce platform or online retail business in Saudi Arabia

steps.label: Activity classification and eligibility verification
steps.description: Classify the e-commerce activity (marketplace operator, direct retailer, or service platform) and verify that the activity is available to foreign investors at MISA. The classification affects which additional registrations and product compliance requirements may apply downstream.
steps.notes: E-commerce is a broad category. Confirm the specific MISA activity code applicable to the intended model before proceeding.

steps.label: Business structure selection
steps.description: Select the legal structure — LLC or branch office. This flow assumes LLC. Verify current requirements for each structure at MISA and the Ministry of Commerce.

steps.label: MISA investment registration
steps.description: Submit an investment registration application to MISA for the authorized e-commerce activity. Successful registration authorizes the investor to establish a Saudi legal entity for the specified activities.

steps.label: Commercial registration
steps.description: Register the legal entity with the Ministry of Commerce to obtain a commercial registration certificate (CR). The CR creates the legal person in the Saudi commercial register.

steps.label: Product compliance assessment (conditional)
steps.description: If the e-commerce business sells regulated product categories — food, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, cosmetics, electronics — identify applicable product registration and conformity requirements. SFDA governs food, pharmaceutical, and medical product registration. Other product categories may have separate conformity frameworks.
steps.notes: This step is conditional on the product categories sold. Technology services and software products typically do not require SFDA registration. Confirm which product categories trigger SFDA or other product-specific requirements.

steps.label: Municipal operating license for physical premises (conditional)
steps.description: If the business maintains physical warehousing, fulfilment centres, or retail locations in Saudi Arabia, obtain a Balady operating license for each premises. Each location requires a separate license.
steps.notes: Applies where physical premises are maintained. A purely digital e-commerce business with no Saudi-based warehousing or retail may not require this step; verify with Balady.

steps.label: Social insurance registration
steps.description: Register as an employer with GOSI before hiring any employees in Saudi Arabia.

steps.label: Tax and zakat registration
steps.description: Register with ZATCA for VAT, zakat, and income tax obligations. E-commerce businesses selling to Saudi consumers are subject to VAT on those sales. Importing goods for sale may also create customs obligations governed by ZATCA.
steps.notes: Confirm current VAT registration thresholds and import/customs requirements at zatca.gov.sa.

steps.label: Labor platform registration and Saudization review
steps.description: Register as an employer on the Qiwa platform (qiwa.sa) before hiring any employees. Authenticate employment contracts via Qiwa. Review Nitaqat obligations before hiring employees. Confirm the applicable Saudization band for e-commerce activities. Register expatriate employee Iqamas via Muqeem within 90 days of arrival.

decision_points.question: What is the e-commerce business model?
options: Marketplace operator — connects third-party sellers and buyers; platform liability and seller compliance obligations may differ from direct retail
Direct retailer — purchases and sells goods directly to Saudi consumers; product compliance and import obligations apply based on product categories
Service platform — digital services delivered online; product registration requirements may not apply; confirm activity code with MISA

decision_points.question: Are regulated product categories involved?
options: Regulated products (food, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, cosmetics) — SFDA product registration and compliance requirements apply before sale
Non-regulated products or digital services — SFDA registration likely not required; verify for the specific product category

decision_points.question: Does the business maintain physical premises in Saudi Arabia?
options: Physical warehousing or retail locations maintained — Balady operating license required per premises
No Saudi-based physical operations — Balady license may not apply; verify registered address requirement

data.name: Manufacturing Company Setup
data.short_description: Conceptual setup sequence for a foreign investor establishing a manufacturing operation in Saudi Arabia, covering the industrial licensing path, site strategy decision, environmental compliance assessment, and product registration considerations.
data.target_investor_type: Foreign investor establishing a manufacturing facility or industrial operation in Saudi Arabia

steps.label: Activity classification and site strategy planning
steps.description: Classify the manufacturing activity under the applicable MISA and Ministry of Industry activity codes, and determine the site strategy: a MODON-operated industrial city or a private premises. This decision affects the premises licensing path (MODON vs. Balady) and may affect infrastructure availability, industrial license processing, and applicable support programs.
steps.notes: MODON industrial cities offer established infrastructure and may streamline certain approvals for eligible industries. A private site provides more location flexibility but requires separate premises licensing with Balady.

steps.label: Activity eligibility verification
steps.description: Verify that the manufacturing activity is available to foreign investors at MISA and that no sector-specific foreign ownership restrictions apply. Confirm the applicable industrial activity code.

steps.label: MISA investment registration
steps.description: Submit an investment registration application to MISA for the authorized manufacturing activity. Successful registration authorizes the investor to establish a Saudi legal entity for the specified industrial activities.

steps.label: Ministry of Industry industrial license
steps.description: Apply for an industrial license from the Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources. The industrial license is the sector-specific authorization for manufacturing activity and is distinct from the commercial registration. It governs the industrial activity classification, applicable standards, and the scope of permitted manufacturing operations.

authority.name: Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources

steps.notes: The industrial license is a primary sector-specific requirement for manufacturing operations. Confirm the application process and documentation requirements at mim.gov.sa.

steps.label: Commercial registration
steps.description: Register the legal entity with the Ministry of Commerce to obtain a commercial registration certificate. The commercial registration creates the legal person; the industrial license governs the manufacturing activity.
steps.notes: The sequencing of commercial registration relative to industrial licensing should be confirmed with both MISA and the Ministry of Industry, as the required order may vary.

steps.label: Premises licensing
steps.description: Obtain a premises operating license from the appropriate authority based on the site strategy decision: a MODON operating license for a facility within a MODON industrial city, or a Balady municipal operating license for a private site. Each manufacturing location requires its own license.

authority.name: MODON (Saudi Authority for Industrial Cities and Technology Zones)

steps.notes: For a private site (outside MODON), the authority is Balady, not MODON. For a MODON industrial city, the licensing authority is MODON. Confirm which industrial cities are relevant to the planned activity at modon.gov.sa.

steps.label: Environmental compliance assessment
steps.description: Assess whether the manufacturing operations generate environmental obligations — emissions, industrial waste, effluent, or land disturbance — that fall within NCEC's scope. If operations meet applicable thresholds, environmental impact assessment and compliance registration with NCEC are required before operations begin.
steps.notes: The NCEC assessment is conditional on the environmental profile of the specific manufacturing activity. Not all manufacturing operations necessarily trigger NCEC involvement. Verify applicable thresholds and requirements at ncec.gov.sa.

steps.label: Product compliance registration (conditional)
steps.description: If the manufactured products fall into regulated categories — food, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, cosmetics, consumer safety products — register products with SFDA or the relevant product authority before sale or distribution in Saudi Arabia.
steps.notes: Conditional on the product category. Industrial components and non-consumer goods typically do not require SFDA registration. Confirm the specific registration requirements for the product category at sfda.gov.sa.

steps.label: Social insurance registration
steps.description: Register as an employer with GOSI before hiring employees.

steps.label: Tax and zakat registration
steps.description: Register with ZATCA for VAT, zakat, income tax, and any applicable customs obligations. Manufacturing businesses importing raw materials have customs obligations governed by ZATCA in addition to the standard tax registration.

steps.label: Labor platform registration and Saudization review
steps.description: Register as an employer on the Qiwa platform (qiwa.sa) before hiring any employees. Authenticate employment contracts via Qiwa. Review Nitaqat obligations. Manufacturing operations are subject to Saudization requirements; the applicable band depends on the industrial activity and workforce size. Register expatriate employee Iqamas via Muqeem within 90 days of arrival.

decision_points.question: MODON industrial city or private site?
options: MODON industrial city — established industrial infrastructure; MODON issues the operating license for the facility; Ministry of Industry governs the activity; may offer access to industrial support programs

Private site outside industrial city — Balady issues the municipal operating license; Ministry of Industry still governs the activity; location is more flexible but infrastructure arrangements are independent

decision_points.question: Do operations generate environmental obligations?
options: Operations generate emissions, waste, effluent, or significant land disturbance — NCEC environmental compliance requirements likely apply; verify thresholds and obtain assessments before commencing operations
Operations have minimal environmental impact — NCEC involvement may not be required; verify applicability based on the specific manufacturing activity

decision_points.question: Are manufactured products in regulated categories?
options: Food, pharmaceutical, medical device, or cosmetics manufacturing — SFDA product registration required before sale or distribution
Industrial components, machinery, or non-consumer products — SFDA registration typically not required; verify for the specific product type

data.name: Fintech Market Entry
data.short_description: Conceptual market entry sequence for a foreign investor entering the Saudi fintech sector, covering regulatory authority determination, the relationship between MISA registration and financial sector licensing, and the distinction between sandbox engagement and full licensing.
data.target_investor_type: Foreign investor entering the Saudi fintech sector — payments, lending, insurance technology, investment platforms, or other regulated financial services

steps.label: Fintech activity classification
steps.description: Classify the fintech activity within the Saudi regulatory framework to determine the primary licensing authority. SAMA regulates payments, banking, insurance, and financing companies. The CMA regulates capital market activities, investment funds, and investment advisory services. Some fintech models intersect both domains.
steps.notes: This classification step is critical because it determines which regulator leads the licensing process. Misclassification can delay the entire market entry. Confirm the applicable regulatory framework before proceeding.

steps.label: Regulatory pathway determination
steps.description: Based on the activity classification, identify whether the primary regulator is SAMA, the CMA, or both. Determine whether the business is eligible for a regulatory sandbox program before a full license application, or must apply directly for the appropriate license.
steps.notes: SAMA operates a fintech regulatory sandbox (SAMA Fintech Lab). CMA operates a regulatory sandbox for capital market innovation. Sandbox participation may be appropriate for early-stage or novel fintech models. Eligibility and availability must be confirmed with the relevant authority.

steps.label: MISA investment registration
steps.description: Submit an investment registration application to MISA for the authorized fintech or financial services activity. MISA investment registration authorizes foreign investor presence for the specified activity scope. For regulated financial activities, the MISA registration and the sector regulator licensing are both required — neither substitutes for the other.
steps.notes: Confirm whether MISA investment registration precedes or runs in parallel with the SAMA or CMA licensing process. The sequencing may vary depending on the specific fintech activity and the regulator's requirements.

steps.label: Regulatory sandbox or license application
steps.description: Submit an application to the primary financial sector regulator (SAMA or CMA) for either sandbox participation or a direct license application. The sandbox pathway allows testing of novel fintech models under regulatory supervision before full licensing. The full license pathway applies to established business models with a defined regulatory framework.
steps.notes: For activities primarily governed by the CMA, the relevant authority for this step is the CMA, not SAMA. For activities requiring both, both regulatory engagement processes apply. Do not assume sandbox participation automatically leads to full licensing.

steps.label: Commercial registration
steps.description: Register the legal entity with the Ministry of Commerce to obtain a commercial registration certificate. For regulated financial services, the timing of commercial registration relative to the sector regulator's licensing process should be confirmed, as the regulator may require a registered legal entity before issuing a license, or may require regulatory approval before commercial registration is finalized.
steps.notes: The required sequence of commercial registration relative to SAMA or CMA licensing varies by activity type. Confirm the required order with the relevant sector regulator.

steps.label: Financial sector license completion
steps.description: Complete the full licensing process with SAMA or CMA as required for the fintech activity. This includes satisfying capital requirements, governance standards, technology infrastructure requirements, and any other conditions imposed by the regulator before full authorization to operate is granted.
steps.notes: Licensing conditions and requirements are set by SAMA and CMA respectively. Do not rely on third-party descriptions of these requirements; confirm current conditions directly with the regulator.

steps.label: Social insurance registration
steps.description: Register as an employer with GOSI before hiring employees in Saudi Arabia.

steps.label: Tax and zakat registration
steps.description: Register with ZATCA for VAT, zakat, and income tax obligations applicable to the fintech business.

steps.label: Labor platform registration and Saudization review
steps.description: Register as an employer on the Qiwa platform (qiwa.sa) before hiring any employees. Authenticate employment contracts via Qiwa. Review Nitaqat obligations before hiring employees. Confirm the applicable Saudization band for financial services or technology activities. Register expatriate employee Iqamas via Muqeem within 90 days of arrival.

steps.label: Ongoing regulatory compliance program
steps.description: Establish internal processes for ongoing compliance with SAMA or CMA regulatory obligations: periodic reporting, capital adequacy monitoring, audit requirements, incident reporting, and any conditions attached to the license. Financial sector regulators impose continuous obligations, not merely a one-time licensing requirement.
steps.notes: Ongoing obligations vary significantly by license type and regulator. This step represents a permanent operational state, not a one-time registration.

decision_points.question: Which regulator governs the primary fintech activity?
options: SAMA — payments, banking, insurance technology, lending, financing companies; SAMA's fintech regulatory framework applies
CMA — investment advisory, capital market platforms, investment funds, securities; CMA's regulatory sandbox and licensing framework applies

Both SAMA and CMA — platforms combining payment services with investment features may require engagement with both regulators; verify the specific activity scope and applicable frameworks with both authorities

decision_points.question: Sandbox participation or direct full license application?
options: Regulatory sandbox — appropriate for novel fintech models, early-stage entrants, or activities without an established licensing precedent; sandbox allows testing under regulatory supervision
Direct full license application — appropriate for established fintech models with a clear regulatory framework; sandbox may not be available for all activity types

decision_points.question: When does commercial registration occur relative to sector licensing?
options: Commercial registration before sector license — check whether the sector regulator requires a registered Saudi legal entity before processing the license application

Sector license approval before or concurrent with commercial registration — some regulatory pathways require regulatory approval as a condition precedent to commercial registration; confirm the required sequence with SAMA or CMA
